'''Henry Frederick''' "'''Fritz'''" '''Schaefer III''' (born June 8, 1944) is an American [[Computational chemistry|computational]], [[Physical chemist|physical]], and [[Theoretical chemistry|theoretical chemist]].<ref>"Leading the Computational Chemistry Field", Scientific Computing World, Aug/Sept 2006, pg 9-11.</ref>

Schaefer is the Graham Perdue Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Georgia]], where he is also the director of its Center for Computational Chemistry.<ref name="CCQCprofilepage">{{cite web |url=http://www.ccqc.uga.edu/people/member_page.php?id=6 |title=Center for Computational Quantum Chemistry Profile Page |work=[[Center for Computational Chemistry]] |publisher=[[University of Georgia]], Athens, Georgia |accessdate=2014-03-25 |archive-date=2020-06-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200618050543/https://www.ccqc.uga.edu/people/member_page.php?id=6 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was previously a professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], and the Wilfred T. Doherty Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Texas at Austin]], where he had been the inaugural director of the Institute for Theoretical Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 11, 2013 |title=Speaker bio: Henry Schaefer |url=https://web.pa.msu.edu/seminars/edge/abstracts/sate-20130524-speaker-bio.pdf |access-date=June 26, 2024 |website=[[Michigan State University]]}}</ref> He is one of the most highly cited chemists in the world, with a [[Thomson Reuters]] [[H-index|''h-''index]] of 121 as of 2020.<ref name="Web of Science">{{cite web |title=Henry F. Schaefer III |url=https://www.ccqc.uga.edu/people/member_page.php?id=6 |accessdate=5 February 2019 |website=CCQC UGA Center for Computational Quantum Chemistry |archive-date=23 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190123223727/https://www.ccqc.uga.edu/people/member_page.php?id=6 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Schaefer is a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], the [[American Physical Society]], the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], the [[American Chemical Society]], and an honorary fellow of the [[Chemical Research Society of India]]. He is the author of more than 1,600 scientific papers and was nominated for the [[Nobel Prize]] on five occasions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Life of a (Christian) Scientist Henry Schaefer {{!}} Department of Environmental Sciences and Policy |url=https://envsci.ceu.edu/events/2016-06-14/life-christian-scientist-henry-f-schaefer-iii |access-date=2024-06-27 |website=[[Central European University]]}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Schaefer was born in [[Grand Rapids, Michigan]], and was raised in [[Syracuse, New York]]; [[Menlo Park, California]]; and [[East Grand Rapids, Michigan]].<ref name="Crawford"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Henry Schaefer - The Godfather |url=https://www.fifteenminuteswith.com/2020/08/28/henry-schaefer-the-godfather/ |website=FifteenMinutesWith |date=28 August 2020 |accessdate=16 March 2021}}</ref> He was one of three children of Henry F. Schaefer Jr. and Janice Christine Trost, both graduates of the [[University of Michigan]]. As a high school student at local Rapids High School, Schaefer met his wife, Karen Rasmussen, and worked as a factory worker for a steel company.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Crawford |first=T. Daniel |date=March 27, 2020 |title=Biography: Henry Frederick Schaefer, III |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/news/henry-frederick-schaefer-iii |access-date=2024-06-26 |website=[[Berkeley College of Chemistry]] |publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]] |language=en}}</ref>

After high school, Schaefer attended the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT), where he initially intended to specialize in [[chemical engineering]]. After deciding to switch to [[chemical physics]], he graduated from MIT with a [[Bachelor of Science]] (B.S.) in the subject in 1966.<ref name=":0" /> He had the opportunity to work with scientists [[George M. Whitesides|George Whitesides]], [[John C. Slater]], [[F. Albert Cotton]], and [[Richard C. Lord]].<ref name="Crawford"/> Walter Thorson, Schaefer's academic advisor at MIT, recommended that he study [[quantum chemistry]] with Thorson's own guidance, under which Schaefer produced his senior thesis on the electronic structure of the compound [[cubane]].<ref name=":0" />

After graduating from MIT, Schaefer was awarded a fellowship from the [[National Defense Education Act]] Fellowship to study chemical physics at [[Stanford University]] and received his [[Ph.D.]] in 1969. At Stanford, he worked with chemist Frank E. Harris on ''[[Ab initio quantum chemistry methods|ab initio]]'' [[electronic structure]] theory and quantum chemistry.<ref name="Crawford">{{cite journal |last1=Crawford |first1=T. Daniel |title=The life and science of Fritz Schaefer |journal=Molecular Physics |date=26 August 2010 |volume=108 |issue=19–20 |pages=2439–2445 |doi=10.1080/00268976.2010.505213 |bibcode=2010MolPh.108.2439C |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Dykstra"/> For his Ph.D. thesis, he examined the electronic structure of first-row atoms and the oxygen molecule.<ref name="Klemm">{{cite journal |last1=Schaefer |first1=Henry F. |last2=Klemm |first2=Richard A. |last3=Harris |first3=Frank E. |title=First-Order Wavefunctions, Orbital Correlation Energies, and Electron Affinities of First-Row Atoms |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |date=15 November 1969 |volume=51 |issue=10 |pages=4643–4650 |doi=10.1063/1.1671837 |bibcode=1969JChPh..51.4643S }}</ref> He published 12 articles in journals including ''Physical Review'' and ''Physical Review Letters'' prior to defending his dissertation.<ref name="Crawford"/>

== Career ==
Schaefer became an assistant professor of [[chemistry]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1969, with access to Berkeley's [[Control Data Corporation]] (CDC) 6600 mainframe computer. Through collaborations with other researchers, he also gained access to resources at the University Computing Company (UCC) in Palo Alto, which had a [[UNIVAC 1108]]. He worked at Berkeley from 1969 to 1987, with one exception. Schaefer spent 1979-1980 as the Wilfred T. Doherty Professor of Chemistry and inaugural Director of the Institute for [[theoretical chemistry|Theoretical Chemistry]] at the [[University of Texas, Austin]], before deciding to return to Berkeley. During his time at Berkeley, Schaefer published 375 papers and several books, including ''The Electronic Structure of Atoms and Molecules: A Survey of Rigorous Quantum Mechanical Results'' (1972) and ''Quantum Chemistry: The Development of Ab Initio Methods in Molecular Electronic Structure Theory'' (1984), a survey of research with commentary.<ref name="Crawford"/>

In August 1987, Schaefer moved to the [[University of Georgia]] as Graham Perdue Professor of Chemistry and director of the newly formed [[Center for Computational Chemistry]]. With the help of an [[IBM 3090|IBM 3090-200E]] mainframe (as well as later models) he and his research group developed various computer-based methods for advanced quantum chemistry.<ref name="Crawford"/>

Other academic appointments include Professeur d'Echange at the [[University of Paris]] (1977), Gastprofessur at the Eidgenössische Technische Hochschule ([[ETH]]), Zurich (1994, 1995, 1997, 2000, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2008, 2010), and David P. Craig Visiting professor at the [[Australian National University]] (1999).<ref name="CV">{{cite web |title=Henry Frederick Schaefer III |url=https://www.ccqc.uga.edu/people/HFS_Vitae.pdf |accessdate=23 January 2019 |website=Center for Computational Quantum Chemistry |archive-date=18 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171118100411/http://www.ccqc.uga.edu/people/HFS_Vitae.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2004, he became Professor of Chemistry Emeritus, at UC Berkeley.<ref name="Rodrigues">{{cite book |last1=Rodrigues |first1=Luís F. |title=Open questions : diverse thinkers discuss God, religion, and faith |date=2010 |publisher=Praeger |isbn=9780313386442 |page=287 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OsGuZjYzXdAC&pg=PA287 |accessdate=23 January 2019}}</ref>

Schaefer became a member of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]] (IAQMS) in 1984.<ref name="IAQMS">{{cite web |title=Henry F. Schaefer III. |url=http://www.iaqms.org/members/schaefer.php |website=International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science |accessdate=23 January 2019}}</ref><ref name="ElectedIA">{{cite news |title=Chemist elected to membership in Academy of Quantum Molecular Science |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2vM2AQAAMAAJ&pg=PA33 |accessdate=23 January 2019|page=23 |work=University Bulletin: A Weekly Bulletin for the Staff of the University of California |volume=33|issue=8|date=October 12, 1984}}</ref> 
He was elected president of [[WATOC]] (World Association of Theoretical and Computational Chemists) in 1996,<ref name="WATOC1997">{{cite news |title=Greetings from the President |url=http://www.ch.ic.ac.uk/watoc/watoc_newsletter_4.html |accessdate=23 January 2019 |work=WATOC Newsletter |issue=1 |date=1997}}</ref> and held the position until 2005.<ref>{{cite web |title=World Association of Theoretical and Computational Chemists |url=http://watoc.net/watoc.history.html |website=WATOC |accessdate=23 January 2019}}</ref> He is also a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] as of 1977,<ref>{{cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive (S) |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=S&year=2012&unit_id=DCP&institution= |website=American Physical Society |accessdate=23 January 2019}}</ref> of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] as of 2002,<ref>{{cite web |title=Elected Fellows |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/listing?field_last_name_value=S&name_combine=&field_institutional_affiliation_value=&field_address_city=All&field_address_administrative_area=All&field_address_country_code=All&field_year_elected=&field_primary_aaas_section=All&page=4 |website=American Association for the Advancement of Science |accessdate=23 January 2019}}</ref>
and of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] as of 2004.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uga.edu/news-bin/artman/exec/view.cgi?archive=7&num=1468&printer=1 |title=UGA chemistry professor Henry F. Schaefer III named Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences |work=Public Affairs News Bureau |publisher=University of Georgia, Athens, Georgia |date=May 5, 2004 |accessdate=2008-02-12}}</ref><ref name="AAAS2004">{{cite web |title=Henry Frederick Schaefer III |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/henry-frederick-schaefer-iii |website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |accessdate=23 January 2019}}</ref>

As of January 2020, Schaefer was the author of more than 1,600 peer-reviewed publications.<ref name="Web of Science"/> A majority of these appeared in the ''[[Journal of Chemical Physics]]'', the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]'', and the ''[[Journal of Physical Chemistry]]''.<ref>Journal of Physical Chemistry, A, Volume 108, No. 15, (2004), pg 2818 - 2840, List of publications of Fritz Schaefer, 1020 are listed to 2004.</ref> He was the editor of ''[[Molecular Physics (journal)|Molecular Physics]]'' for 11 years. He has directed 123 Ph.D. students, as well as many postdoctoral associates and visiting professors, now working at 42 academic institutions around the world.<ref name="Web of Science"/>

In 2023, Schaefer was the eighth highest paid faculty member at the University of Georgia, with a salary of $430,140.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Countryman |first=Vanessa |date=August 5, 2024 |title=Leading the Dawgs: UGA's top 20 highest paid faculty members |url=https://www.onlineathens.com/story/news/2024/08/05/who-are-ugas-highest-paid-faculty-and-what-do-they-do/74616525007/ |work=[[Athens Banner-Herald]]}}</ref>

== Research ==
Research within the Schaefer group involves the use of computational hardware and theoretical methods to solve problems in molecular [[quantum mechanics]]. His contributions to the field of [[quantum chemistry]] include a paper challenging, on theoretical grounds, the geometry of triplet methylene as assigned by Nobel Prize-winning experimentalist [[Gerhard Herzberg]]; the development of the Z-vector method simplifying certain calculations of correlated systems; and a wide body of work undertaken in his research group on the geometries, properties, and reactions of chemical systems using highly accurate ''ab initio'' quantum chemical techniques. Many of these papers have predicted, or forced a reinterpretation of, experimental results.<ref name="Crawford"/><ref name="Dykstra"/>

===Awards and honors===
[[File:H F Schafer.jpg|right|thumb | Schaefer in 2009]]
Schaefer was awarded the American Chemical Society's [[ACS Award in Pure Chemistry]] in 1979<ref name="ACSAward">{{cite web |title=ACS Award in Pure Chemistry |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/acs-award-in-pure-chemistry.html |website=ACS Chemistry for Life |accessdate=23 January 2019}}</ref> "for the development of computational quantum chemistry into a reliable quantitative field of chemistry and for prolific exemplary calculations of broad chemical interest".<ref name="Science_Christianity">{{cite book |last=Schaefer |first=Henry F. |title=Science and Christianity: Conflict or Coherence? |publisher=The Apollos Trust |year=2003 |isbn=978-0-9742975-0-7 |authorlink=Henry F. Schaefer III}} An expanded fifth printing appeared in 2008</ref>{{rp|183}} The Pure Chemistry Award is given to the outstanding chemist in America under the age of 35. In 1983, he received the [[Leo Hendrik Baekeland]] award for the most distinguished North American chemist under the age of 40. In 1992, he was awarded the [[Centenary Prize]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], London, for being "the first theoretical chemist successfully to challenge the accepted conclusion of a distinguished experimental group for a polyatomic molecule, namely methylene."<ref>The Royal Society of Chemistry publication article: "Endowed Lecturers," ''Chemistry in Britain'', vol. 28, no. 9, (September 1992), 837.</ref>

In 2003, Schaefer received the American Chemical Society Award in Theoretical Chemistry and the [[Ira Remsen#Remsen Award|Ira Remsen Award]] of Johns Hopkins University.<ref name="Dykstra">{{cite journal |last1=Dykstra |first1=CE |last2=Garrison |first2=BJ |last3=Scuseria |first3=GE |title=Biography of Fritz Schaefer |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry A |date=April 2004 |volume=108 |issue=15 |pages=2805–2807 |doi=10.1021/jp040037w |bibcode=2004JPCA..108.2805. }}</ref> In 2004, a six-day conference was convened in [[Gyeongju, Korea]] on the “Theory and Applications of Computational Chemistry: A Celebration of 1000 Papers of Professor Henry F. Schaefer III.”<ref>{{cite web |title=Theory and Applications of Computational Chemistry: A Celebration of 1000 Papers of Professor Henry F. Schaefer III, Kwang S. Kim et al. |url=http://www.tc.bham.ac.uk/~roy/TCG/tacc.pdf |website=University of Birmingham |accessdate=23 January 2019}}</ref> Schaefer was honored with the $10,000 [[Joseph O. Hirschfelder]] Prize in 2005 by the University of Wisconsin's Theoretical Chemistry Institute.<ref name="hirschfelder">{{cite web |title=Joseph O. Hirschfelder Prize |url=https://www.chem.wisc.edu/content/joseph-o-hirschfelder-prize |website=University of Wisconsin |accessdate=23 January 2019 |archive-date=4 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180704034654/https://www.chem.wisc.edu/content/joseph-o-hirschfelder-prize |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2011, Schaefer received the Ide P. Trotter Prize from Texas A&M University.<ref>{{cite web |title=Trotter Prize & Endowed Lecture Series |url=http://www.science.tamu.edu/trotter/ |website=Science Texas A&M University |accessdate=23 January 2019}}</ref> 
In 2012, he received a [[Humboldt Prize|Humboldt Research Award]] from the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] in Germany,<ref name="Fahmy">{{cite news |last1=Fahmy |first1=Sam |title=Renowned UGA chemist Henry Schaefer honored with Humboldt Research Award |url=https://news.uga.edu/renowned-uga-chemist-henry-schaefer-honored-with-humboldt-research-awa/ |accessdate=23 January 2019 |work=UGA Today |date=November 30, 2011}}</ref> and on March 29, 2012, he received the $20,000 SURA Distinguished Scientist Award from the [[Southeastern Universities Research Association]] for fulfilling SURA's mission of fostering excellence in scientific research.<ref name="Hataway">{{cite news |last1=Hataway |first1=James |title=Noted UGA chemist named SURA distinguished scientist |url=https://news.uga.edu/noted-uga-chemist-named-sura-distinguished-scientist/ |accessdate=23 January 2019 |work=UGA Today |date=March 22, 2012}}</ref>

In 2013, Schaefer received the [[Chemical Pioneer Award]] of the [[American Institute of Chemists]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theaic.org/award_winners/chem_pioneer.html#cpa00s|title=Chemical Pioneer Award Winners|publisher= American Institute of Chemists|accessdate = 16 May 2018}}</ref> On March 18, 2014, Schaefer received the [[American Chemical Society]] [[Peter Debye Award]] in [[Physical Chemistry]].<ref name="Debye"/> In March 2015, Schaefer was elected as an Honorary Fellow of the Chemical Research Society of India. He returned to India to give his CRSI Honorary Fellow award lecture on February 6, 2016, at Panjab University in Chandigarh.<ref name="CCQC">{{cite web |title=Professor Henry F. Schaefer |url=https://www.ccqc.uga.edu/people/member_page.php?id=6 |website=Center for Computational Quantum Chemistry |accessdate=23 January 2019 |archive-date=23 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190123223727/https://www.ccqc.uga.edu/people/member_page.php?id=6 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Schaefer received the [[American Institute of Chemists Gold Medal]] on May 8, 2019.<ref name="Gempf">{{cite news |last1=Gempf |first1=Kathryn L. |title=PCCP Associate Editor Henry F. Schaefer III awarded American Institute of Chemists Gold Award |url=http://blogs.rsc.org/cp/2019/01/15/pccp-associate-editor-henry-f-schaefer-iii-awarded-american-institute-of-chemists-gold-award/?doing_wp_cron=1548262092.9345479011535644531250 |accessdate=23 January 2019 |work=PCCP Blog |date=15 Jan 2019}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Schaefer married Karen Rasmussen, a graduate of [[Wells College]] and [[Stanford University]], on September 2, 1966.<ref name=":0" /> He is an outspoken Christian, and has described himself as sympathetic to teleological arguments, but is primarily a "proponent of Jesus."<ref>{{cite web |title=Henry F. Schaefer, III |url=https://www.doesgodexist.org/Journals--2017/4thQtr17/Schaefer--Scientists.html |accessdate=23 January 2019 |website=Does God Exist? |archive-date=23 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190123223418/https://www.doesgodexist.org/Journals--2017/4thQtr17/Schaefer--Scientists.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Religion and science ===
Schaefer is an active [[Protestant]] [[Christians|Christian]] educator who regularly speaks to university audiences, Christian groups and the public on science/faith issues.<ref name="Science_Christianity" /> In 2003, he published ''Science and Christianity: Conflict or Coherence?'', a collection of essays and talks on the subject.<ref name="Science_Christianity" /> A second edition appeared in 2016. He is a member of the Christian Faculty Forum at the University of Georgia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Henry F. Schaefer, III |url=http://cffatuga.com/faculty/henry-f-schaefer-iii/ |accessdate=23 January 2019 |website=Christian Faculty Forum}}</ref> Schaefer wrote the forward to [[William A. Dembski]]'s 1998 book ''Mere Creation: Science, Faith and Intelligent Design''.<ref name=":12">Henry F. Schaefer III, “Foreword,” in Mere Creation: Science, Faith and Intelligent Design, William A. Dembski, Ed. (Downers Grove, Ill.: InterVarsity Press, 1998), 9.</ref> 

Schaefer is a proponent of [[intelligent design]]<ref name=":12"/><ref>{{Cite news |last=Krishna |first=R |date=November 19, 2013 |title=Some IIT students fail to see the Intelligence in Schaefer's Design |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/speak-up/report-some-iit-students-fail-to-see-the-intelligence-in-schaefer-s-design-1147616 |work=[[Daily News and Analysis]]}}</ref> and a fellow of the [[Discovery Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 25, 2004 |title=Discovery Institute Fellow Elected to Prestigious American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.discovery.org/a/2052/ |website=[[Discovery Institute]]}}</ref>
